title: Termwise bound bounds the list maximum
statement: Let $s$ be a finite list of natural numbers and let $n$ be a natural number. If every member of $s$ is at most $n$, then the right fold of maximum over $s$, with initial value $0$, is at most $n$.
replaced:
Let $s$ be a finite list of natural numbers, write $\max(s)$ for the right fold of
$\max$ over $s$ with initial value $0$, and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. If every member of
$s$ is at most $n$, then $\max(s) \le n$; in particular this holds when $s$ is empty.
